paragraphs: Children in care in Liverpool are looked after by Liverpool City Council's fostering service and by the independent agencies listed on this page. In April 2023 the council appealed for more residents to foster, saying the number of looked-after children in the city had risen by 31% since 2017 while foster carer numbers had not kept pace.

Liverpool is one of eight councils across Cheshire and Merseyside, led by Warrington, that were awarded new fostering funding in December 2023: more than £1 million for a larger shared recruitment hub, Foster4, and £1 million to extend the Mockingbird programme, in which an experienced hub carer supports a group of nearby fostering families.

To foster with the council you need to be over 21, have a spare room and live in the UK full-time. You can be single or married, of any gender or sexual orientation, own or rent your home, and have children or pets of your own. After a first call and a home visit, applicants take the two-day Skills to Foster course, then complete a full assessment with references, medical and police checks before going to the fostering panel. The council says this usually takes three to six months.

Approved carers have a named fostering social worker, training matched to the children they look after, family support workers and local support groups. The council has also listed free Lifestyles gym membership and Council Tax relief among its benefits, alongside child allowances and carer payments.
If you live in Liverpool, speak to the council and two or three of the agencies below, and compare their training, support and pay before you decide.
